The pull request backstop checks review only when a task or fix is marked done. A task pull request can be opened and merged before `forge close` marks it done, so the specified checks do not make mandatory review unbypassable (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:202-203, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:543-547, docs/decisions/0092-close-is-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:29-36).

The generated host-hook commands have no specified blocking behavior when `forge` cannot launch. The retained portable-hook decision documents that a non-2 launch failure can leave a Claude hook non-blocking and requires an executable health check, while this doctor contract checks drift and installed shims only (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:290-319, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:384-390, docs/decisions/0038-portable-fail-closed-hooks.md:12-19, docs/decisions/0038-portable-fail-closed-hooks.md:22-46).

No command or trigger marks a story done or writes its done date after all task pull requests merge, although story state, the board timeline and success measures require that transition (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:71-88, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:326-328, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:345-352, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:605-609).

Client migration says the copied manifest identifies the files to delete, but the current manifest records only gate trees and three gate files; it does not inventory the listed docs, workflows, constitution or Codex roles. The deletion set and ownership test are therefore undefined for those paths (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:400-407, factory/scripts/check_vendor_integrity.py:23-25, factory/scripts/check_vendor_integrity.py:46-68).

Migration explicitly deletes client-modified copied files and reports their names only after the change. It specifies no preflight ownership check, preservation or recovery for client additions in mixed-ownership paths, despite the current vendoring contract protecting client skills and workflows (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:400-407, docs/specs/harness-owned-vendoring.md:30-39, factory/scripts/forge_cli/scaffold.py:25-37).

Migration does not specify a contained preflight for every write and delete, or an interrupted-run retry rule. Those are material for a command removing trees in a client repository under the still-binding path-boundary decision (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:394-416, docs/decisions/0028-path-boundary-invariant.md:37-63, docs/decisions/0093-lean-forge-rebuild.md:126-132).

Carrying an old plan's approval and done-task status is specified only as a conversion result. The source records to trust, how to prove the approved sections are unchanged, and how done tasks survive deletion of old `.factory/` records are not defined (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:400-415).

Source-repo migration and sign-off exemption are selected by the presence of `src/forge/`. A client product could have that path; the spec gives no stronger repository identity check before choosing the delete-nothing mode and bypassing client sign-off (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:156-159, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:422-424).

The proposed success baseline is for close after a clean build, while the target cycle-time metric starts at `forge task start`. No comparable baseline for that metric is supplied (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:605-618).

The principle and criterion say gates refuse only for outcome failures, but the same spec requires refusals for version mismatch, malformed story tables, unrecognized branches and fix file limits (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:26, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:64-65, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:189-194, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:464-469, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:499-502, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:530-538).

The first spec and roadmap cannot be committed through the stated lanes: default-branch commits and branches Forge did not start are refused; a fix touching `docs/specs/` is refused; and a story cannot start without an existing roadmap key (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:79-86, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:119-120, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:189-194, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:277-280).

`forge init` runs `forge sync`, which installs a pre-commit hook refusing default-branch commits, while acceptance criterion 9 requires `forge init` to make the first commit in a repo with no commits. No first-commit exception is given for that hook (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:73-74, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:272-280, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:489-493).

Codex approval is required through `request_user_input`, but the still-binding host-interaction decision says Default mode forbids that tool for required approvals and directs the coordinator to ask in ordinary chat. This approval path cannot run under the stated host rules (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:149-154, docs/decisions/0061-host-native-human-interaction.md:17-29, docs/decisions/0093-lean-forge-rebuild.md:126-133).

The spec permits edits to Why, Tasks and Notes without new approval, but its roadmap acceptance check rejects a story doc whose approval hash does not match the doc. A whole-doc hash would reject those permitted edits; a sections-only hash cannot satisfy the wording of that check (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:144-145, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:460-463, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:505-506).

Human touches are counted in the shared story state file, while the spec says each parallel branch writes only its own state file. The human may overrule the fix lane and keep work under the limit, but the specified pre-commit and pre-push hooks always refuse a fix that exceeds that limit. No overruling input or exception is defined for the hooks (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:189-198, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:277-285).

The confirmed close rule requires a committed review result containing findings and dismissals. The specified event order and date order disagree unless a separate post-merge story transition is added (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:202-203, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:225-229, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:349-352).

findings: The promise that every story removes at least as much process as it adds has no measure or gate. The specified CI checks enforce only module length and command count (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:29, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:475-477).

There is no specified route to derive the first roadmap from confirmed specs, although story creation requires a roadmap key. The retained sign-off decision requires a derived roadmap covering every confirmed spec (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:73-86, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:119-120, docs/decisions/0014-specs-before-signoff.md:21-26).

Spec confirmation has no cold-read requirement in this design, although the retained sign-off contract requires a fresh passing spec grill before confirmation (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:85, docs/decisions/0014-specs-before-signoff.md:23-26).

The story cold read must flag unlisted one-way steps, but the required story-doc shape has no Risks section or defined place to resolve that finding (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:92-117, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:135-141).

The cold read is called read-only, but no enforceable read-only boundary is specified for the worker backend that can otherwise edit and commit in a worktree (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:126-128, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:177-178).

The cold read records only the document hash as read. The spec does not define how the amended hash and complete finding dispositions are validated before approval, despite the confirmed close contract requiring both read and amended hashes (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:126-128, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:138-145, docs/specs/close-on-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:50-54, docs/specs/close-on-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:106-107).

Approval capture does not specify the retained Codex trust checks for the exact current digest, runtime, tool identity, replay refusal and one eligible candidate. Matching a short hash alone leaves those required checks to the implementer to guess (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:149-154, docs/decisions/0082-codex-hook-trust-boundary.md:17-22).

The story doc, read notes and approval state are written in a story worktree, but no step commits them before task branches are created from the story branch. An uncommitted story doc cannot reach the first task pull request by branching from that branch (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:119-128, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:165-170).

A task row has no declared write scope, required tests or explicit mapping from its deliverable to Done-when items. Parallel task start has no rule for overlapping changes, branch refresh or reconciliation after one task merges. Dependency readiness alone cannot establish that two task branches can merge safely (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:165-171).

The fix lane supplies only a one-line reason, yet fixes close by the same review rule as tasks. The spec never says what acceptance or test instructions let a reviewer decide that a fix is done (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:184-188, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:202-211, docs/specs/close-on-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:77-92).

The promote rule depends on optional `interfaces` globs, defaulting to an empty list, with no default definition of an interface. An API or data-contract change can therefore remain a fix despite the accepted decision requiring interface changes to become stories (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:61, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:189-194, docs/decisions/0093-lean-forge-rebuild.md:40-42).

Promotion requires a roadmap key, but no route is specified for adding a newly discovered fix to the roadmap before `forge story new <KEY> --from-fix` can run (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:119-120, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:194-196).

A nonempty `checks` list is insufficient to establish the required full test suite. The pull request backstop checks review only when a task or fix is marked done. A task pull request can be opened and merged before `forge close` marks it done, so the specified checks do not make mandatory review unbypassable (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:202-203, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:543-547, docs/decisions/0092-close-is-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:29-36).

The generated host-hook commands have no specified blocking behavior when `forge` cannot launch. The retained portable-hook decision documents that a non-2 launch failure can leave a Claude hook non-blocking and requires an executable health check, while this doctor contract checks drift and installed shims only (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:290-319, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:384-390, docs/decisions/0038-portable-fail-closed-hooks.md:12-19, docs/decisions/0038-portable-fail-closed-hooks.md:22-46).

No command or trigger marks a story done or writes its done date after all task pull requests merge, although story state, the board timeline and success measures require that transition (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:71-88, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:326-328, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:345-352, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:605-609).

Client migration says the copied manifest identifies the files to delete, but the current manifest records only gate trees and three gate files; it does not inventory the listed docs, workflows, constitution or Codex roles. The deletion set and ownership test are therefore undefined for those paths (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:400-407, factory/scripts/check_vendor_integrity.py:23-25, factory/scripts/check_vendor_integrity.py:46-68).

Migration explicitly deletes client-modified copied files and reports their names only after the change. It specifies no preflight ownership check, preservation or recovery for client additions in mixed-ownership paths, despite the current vendoring contract protecting client skills and workflows (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:400-407, docs/specs/harness-owned-vendoring.md:30-39, factory/scripts/forge_cli/scaffold.py:25-37).

Migration does not specify a contained preflight for every write and delete, or an interrupted-run retry rule. Those are material for a command removing trees in a client repository under the still-binding path-boundary decision (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:394-416, docs/decisions/0028-path-boundary-invariant.md:37-63, docs/decisions/0093-lean-forge-rebuild.md:126-132).

Carrying an old plan's approval and done-task status is specified only as a conversion result. The source records to trust, how to prove the approved sections are unchanged, and how done tasks survive deletion of old `.factory/` records are not defined (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:400-415).

Source-repo migration and sign-off exemption are selected by the presence of `src/forge/`. A client product could have that path; the spec gives no stronger repository identity check before choosing the delete-nothing mode and bypassing client sign-off (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:156-159, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:422-424).

The proposed success baseline is for close after a clean build, while the target cycle-time metric starts at `forge task start`. No comparable baseline for that metric is supplied (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:605-618).

The principle and criterion say gates refuse only for outcome failures, but the same spec requires refusals for version mismatch, malformed story tables, unrecognized branches and fix file limits (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:26, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:64-65, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:189-194, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:464-469, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:499-502, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:530-538).

The first spec and roadmap cannot be committed through the stated lanes: default-branch commits and branches Forge did not start are refused; a fix touching `docs/specs/` is refused; and a story cannot start without an existing roadmap key (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:79-86, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:119-120, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:189-194, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:277-280).

This approval path cannot run under the stated host rules (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:149-154, docs/decisions/0061-host-native-human-interaction.md:17-29, docs/decisions/0093-lean-forge-rebuild.md:126-133).

Spec confirmation has no cold-read requirement in this design, although the retained sign-off contract requires a fresh passing spec grill before confirmation (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:85, docs/decisions/0014-specs-before-signoff.md:23-26).

The story cold read must flag unlisted one-way steps, but the required story-doc shape has no Risks section or defined place to resolve that finding (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:92-117, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:135-141).

The cold read is called read-only, but no enforceable read-only boundary is specified for the worker backend that can otherwise edit and commit in a worktree (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:126-128, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:177-178).

The cold read records only the document hash as read. The spec does not define how the amended hash and complete finding dispositions are validated before approval, despite the confirmed close contract requiring both read and amended hashes (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:126-128, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:138-145, docs/specs/close-on-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:50-54, docs/specs/close-on-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:106-107).

Approval capture does not specify the retained Codex trust checks for the exact current digest, runtime, tool identity, replay refusal and one eligible candidate. Matching a short hash alone leaves those required checks to the implementer to guess (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:149-154, docs/decisions/0082-codex-hook-trust-boundary.md:17-22).

The story doc, read notes and approval state are written in a story worktree, but no step commits them before task branches are created from the story branch. An uncommitted story doc cannot reach the first task pull request by branching from that branch (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:119-128, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:165-170).

A task row has no declared write scope, required tests or explicit mapping from its deliverable to Done-when items. Parallel task start has no rule for overlapping changes, branch refresh or reconciliation after one task merges. Dependency readiness alone cannot establish that two task branches can merge safely (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:165-171).

The fix lane supplies only a one-line reason, yet fixes close by the same review rule as tasks. The spec never says what acceptance or test instructions let a reviewer decide that a fix is done (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:184-188, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:202-211, docs/specs/close-on-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:77-92).

The promote rule depends on optional `interfaces` globs, defaulting to an empty list, with no default definition of an interface. An API or data-contract change can therefore remain a fix despite the accepted decision requiring interface changes to become stories (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:61, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:189-194, docs/decisions/0093-lean-forge-rebuild.md:40-42).

Promotion requires a roadmap key, but no route is specified for adding a newly discovered fix to the roadmap before `forge story new <KEY> --from-fix` can run (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:119-120, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:194-196).

The pull request backstop checks review only when a task or fix is marked done. The generated host-hook commands have no specified blocking behavior when `forge` cannot launch. The retained portable-hook decision documents that a non-2 launch failure can leave a Claude hook non-blocking and requires an executable health check, while this doctor contract checks drift and installed shims only (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:290-319, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:384-390, docs/decisions/0038-portable-fail-closed-hooks.md:12-19, docs/decisions/0038-portable-fail-closed-hooks.md:22-46).

No command or trigger marks a story done or writes its done date after all task pull requests merge, although story state, the board timeline and success measures require that transition (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:71-88, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:326-328, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:345-352, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:605-609).

Client migration says the copied manifest identifies the files to delete, but the current manifest records only gate trees and three gate files; it does not inventory the listed docs, workflows, constitution or Codex roles. The deletion set and ownership test are therefore undefined for those paths (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:400-407, factory/scripts/check_vendor_integrity.py:23-25, factory/scripts/check_vendor_integrity.py:46-68).

Migration explicitly deletes client-modified copied files and reports their names only after the change. It specifies no preflight ownership check, preservation or recovery for client additions in mixed-ownership paths, despite the current vendoring contract protecting client skills and workflows (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:400-407, docs/specs/harness-owned-vendoring.md:30-39, factory/scripts/forge_cli/scaffold.py:25-37).

Carrying an old plan's approval and done-task status is specified only as a conversion result. The source records to trust, how to prove the approved sections are unchanged, and how done tasks survive deletion of old `.factory/` records are not defined (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:400-415).

Source-repo migration and sign-off exemption are selected by the presence of `src/forge/`. The proposed success baseline is for close after a clean build, while the target cycle-time metric starts at `forge task start`. No comparable baseline for that metric is supplied (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:605-618).

Human touches are counted in the shared story state file, while the spec says each parallel branch writes only its own state file. It also counts answered questions in the story worktree even though implementation runs in task worktrees, leaving task questions uncounted (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:160-167, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:324-337, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:512-513).

The human may overrule the fix lane and keep work under the limit, but the specified pre-commit and pre-push hooks always refuse a fix that exceeds that limit. No overruling input or exception is defined for the hooks (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:189-198, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:277-285).

The confirmed close rule requires a committed review result containing findings and dismissals. The v1 state file retains only commit, product tree and clean/blocked status, putting findings and dismissals solely in a mutable pull request body (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:222-224, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:329-337, docs/specs/close-on-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:33-40, docs/specs/close-on-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:80-89).

findings: The promise that every story removes at least as much process as it adds has no measure or gate. The specified CI checks enforce only module length and command count (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:29, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:475-477).

There is no specified route to derive the first roadmap from confirmed specs, although story creation requires a roadmap key. The retained sign-off decision requires a derived roadmap covering every confirmed spec (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:73-86, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:119-120, docs/decisions/0014-specs-before-signoff.md:21-26).

Spec confirmation has no cold-read requirement in this design, although the retained sign-off contract requires a fresh passing spec grill before confirmation (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:85, docs/decisions/0014-specs-before-signoff.md:23-26).

The story cold read must flag unlisted one-way steps, but the required story-doc shape has no Risks section or defined place to resolve that finding (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:92-117, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:135-141).

The cold read is called read-only, but no enforceable read-only boundary is specified for the worker backend that can otherwise edit and commit in a worktree (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:126-128, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:177-178).

The cold read records only the document hash as read. The spec does not define how the amended hash and complete finding dispositions are validated before approval, despite the confirmed close contract requiring both read and amended hashes (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:126-128, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:138-145, docs/specs/close-on-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:50-54, docs/specs/close-on-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:106-107).

Approval capture does not specify the retained Codex trust checks for the exact current digest, runtime, tool identity, replay refusal and one eligible candidate. Matching a short hash alone leaves those required checks to the implementer to guess (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:149-154, docs/decisions/0082-codex-hook-trust-boundary.md:17-22).

The story doc, read notes and approval state are written in a story worktree, but no step commits them before task branches are created from the story branch. An uncommitted story doc cannot reach the first task pull request by branching from that branch (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:119-128, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:165-170).

A task row has no declared write scope, required tests or explicit mapping from its deliverable to Done-when items. Close is nevertheless required to give Autoreview the task's scope and required-test audit instructions (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:100-116, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:172-175, docs/specs/close-on-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:33-36, docs/specs/close-on-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:90-92).

Parallel task start has no rule for overlapping changes, branch refresh or reconciliation after one task merges. Dependency readiness alone cannot establish that two task branches can merge safely (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:165-171).

The fix lane supplies only a one-line reason, yet fixes close by the same review rule as tasks. The spec never says what acceptance or test instructions let a reviewer decide that a fix is done (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:184-188, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:202-211, docs/specs/close-on-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:77-92).

The promote rule depends on optional `interfaces` globs, defaulting to an empty list, with no default definition of an interface. An API or data-contract change can therefore remain a fix despite the accepted decision requiring interface changes to become stories (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:61, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:189-194, docs/decisions/0093-lean-forge-rebuild.md:40-42).

Promotion requires a roadmap key, but no route is specified for adding a newly discovered fix to the roadmap before `forge story new <KEY> --from-fix` can run (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:119-120, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:194-196).

A nonempty `checks` list is insufficient to establish the required full test suite. The pull request backstop checks review only when a task or fix is marked done. A task pull request can be opened and merged before `forge close` marks it done, so the specified checks do not make mandatory review unbypassable (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:202-203, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:543-547, docs/decisions/0092-close-is-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:29-36).

The generated host-hook commands have no specified blocking behavior when `forge` cannot launch. The retained portable-hook decision documents that a non-2 launch failure can leave a Claude hook non-blocking and requires an executable health check, while this doctor contract checks drift and installed shims only (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:290-319, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:384-390, docs/decisions/0038-portable-fail-closed-hooks.md:12-19, docs/decisions/0038-portable-fail-closed-hooks.md:22-46).

No command or trigger marks a story done or writes its done date after all task pull requests merge, although story state, the board timeline and success measures require that transition (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:71-88, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:326-328, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:345-352, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:605-609).

Client migration says the copied manifest identifies the files to delete, but the current manifest records only gate trees and three gate files; it does not inventory the listed docs, workflows, constitution or Codex roles. The deletion set and ownership test are therefore undefined for those paths (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:400-407, factory/scripts/check_vendor_integrity.py:23-25, factory/scripts/check_vendor_integrity.py:46-68).

Migration explicitly deletes client-modified copied files and reports their names only after the change. It specifies no preflight ownership check, preservation or recovery for client additions in mixed-ownership paths, despite the current vendoring contract protecting client skills and workflows (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:400-407, docs/specs/harness-owned-vendoring.md:30-39, factory/scripts/forge_cli/scaffold.py:25-37).

Carrying an old plan's approval and done-task status is specified only as a conversion result. The source records to trust, how to prove the approved sections are unchanged, and how done tasks survive deletion of old `.factory/` records are not defined (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:400-415).

Source-repo migration and sign-off exemption are selected by the presence of `src/forge/`. The proposed success baseline is for close after a clean build, while the target cycle-time metric starts at `forge task start`. No comparable baseline for that metric is supplied (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:605-618).

The principle and criterion say gates refuse only for outcome failures, but the same spec requires refusals for version mismatch, malformed story tables, unrecognized branches and fix file limits (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:26, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:64-65, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:189-194, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:464-469, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:499-502, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:530-538).

`forge init` runs `forge sync`, which installs a pre-commit hook refusing default-branch commits, while acceptance criterion 9 requires `forge init` to make the first commit in a repo with no commits. No first-commit exception is given for that hook (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:73-74, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:272-280, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:489-493).

Codex approval is required through `request_user_input`, but the still-binding host-interaction decision says Default mode forbids that tool for required approvals and directs the coordinator to ask in ordinary chat. This approval path cannot run under the stated host rules (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:149-154, docs/decisions/0061-host-native-human-interaction.md:17-29, docs/decisions/0093-lean-forge-rebuild.md:126-133).

The spec permits edits to Why, Tasks and Notes without new approval, but its roadmap acceptance check rejects a story doc whose approval hash does not match the doc. A whole-doc hash would reject those permitted edits; a sections-only hash cannot satisfy the wording of that check (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:144-145, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:460-463, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:505-506).

Each Done-when item is made an instruction to the reviewer, and every task brief carries the entire Done-when list. The confirmed close rule requires unmet items to be P1 findings, so the first task of a multi-task story would be blocked by items assigned to later tasks (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:108-116, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:172-174, docs/specs/close-on-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:77-79).

Human touches are counted in the shared story state file, while the spec says each parallel branch writes only its own state file. It also counts answered questions in the story worktree even though implementation runs in task worktrees, leaving task questions uncounted (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:160-167, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:324-337, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:512-513).

The human may overrule the fix lane and keep work under the limit, but the specified pre-commit and pre-push hooks always refuse a fix that exceeds that limit. No overruling input or exception is defined for the hooks (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:189-198, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:277-285).

The confirmed close rule requires a committed review result containing findings and dismissals. The v1 state file retains only commit, product tree and clean/blocked status, putting findings and dismissals solely in a mutable pull request body (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:222-224, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:329-337, docs/specs/close-on-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:33-40, docs/specs/close-on-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:80-89).

Close marks an item done after CI while a human merges later, but the board timeline puts each merge before 'The story was finished' on the done date. The specified event order and date order disagree unless a separate post-merge story transition is added (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:202-203, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:225-229, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:349-352).

`forge migrate` uses `forge/migrate-v1` and says it ends through normal close, but the hooks refuse branches without story, task or fix state, and `forge close` is defined only for a task or fix. findings: The promise that every story removes at least as much process as it adds has no measure or gate. The specified CI checks enforce only module length and command count (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:29, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:475-477).

There is no specified route to derive the first roadmap from confirmed specs, although story creation requires a roadmap key. Spec confirmation has no cold-read requirement in this design, although the retained sign-off contract requires a fresh passing spec grill before confirmation (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:85, docs/decisions/0014-specs-before-signoff.md:23-26).

The story cold read must flag unlisted one-way steps, but the required story-doc shape has no Risks section or defined place to resolve that finding (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:92-117, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:135-141).

The cold read is called read-only, but no enforceable read-only boundary is specified for the worker backend that can otherwise edit and commit in a worktree (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:126-128, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:177-178).

The cold read records only the document hash as read. The spec does not define how the amended hash and complete finding dispositions are validated before approval, despite the confirmed close contract requiring both read and amended hashes (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:126-128, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:138-145, docs/specs/close-on-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:50-54, docs/specs/close-on-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:106-107).

Approval capture does not specify the retained Codex trust checks for the exact current digest, runtime, tool identity, replay refusal and one eligible candidate. Matching a short hash alone leaves those required checks to the implementer to guess (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:149-154, docs/decisions/0082-codex-hook-trust-boundary.md:17-22).

The story doc, read notes and approval state are written in a story worktree, but no step commits them before task branches are created from the story branch. An uncommitted story doc cannot reach the first task pull request by branching from that branch (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:119-128, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:165-170).

A task row has no declared write scope, required tests or explicit mapping from its deliverable to Done-when items. Parallel task start has no rule for overlapping changes, branch refresh or reconciliation after one task merges. Dependency readiness alone cannot establish that two task branches can merge safely (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:165-171).

The fix lane supplies only a one-line reason, yet fixes close by the same review rule as tasks. The spec never says what acceptance or test instructions let a reviewer decide that a fix is done (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:184-188, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:202-211, docs/specs/close-on-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:77-92).

The promote rule depends on optional `interfaces` globs, defaulting to an empty list, with no default definition of an interface. An API or data-contract change can therefore remain a fix despite the accepted decision requiring interface changes to become stories (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:61, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:189-194, docs/decisions/0093-lean-forge-rebuild.md:40-42).

Promotion requires a roadmap key, but no route is specified for adding a newly discovered fix to the roadmap before `forge story new <KEY> --from-fix` can run (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:119-120, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:194-196).

The generated host-hook commands have no specified blocking behavior when `forge` cannot launch. No command or trigger marks a story done or writes its done date after all task pull requests merge, although story state, the board timeline and success measures require that transition (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:71-88, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:326-328, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:345-352, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:605-609).

Client migration says the copied manifest identifies the files to delete, but the current manifest records only gate trees and three gate files; it does not inventory the listed docs, workflows, constitution or Codex roles. The deletion set and ownership test are therefore undefined for those paths (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:400-407, factory/scripts/check_vendor_integrity.py:23-25, factory/scripts/check_vendor_integrity.py:46-68).

The proposed success baseline is for close after a clean build, while the target cycle-time metric starts at `forge task start`. No comparable baseline for that metric is supplied (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:605-618).

The principle and criterion say gates refuse only for outcome failures, but the same spec requires refusals for version mismatch, malformed story tables, unrecognized branches and fix file limits (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:26, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:64-65, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:189-194, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:464-469, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:499-502, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:530-538).

The first spec and roadmap cannot be committed through the stated lanes: default-branch commits and branches Forge did not start are refused; a fix touching `docs/specs/` is refused; and a story cannot start without an existing roadmap key (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:79-86, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:119-120, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:189-194, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:277-280).

`forge init` runs `forge sync`, which installs a pre-commit hook refusing default-branch commits, while acceptance criterion 9 requires `forge init` to make the first commit in a repo with no commits. No first-commit exception is given for that hook (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:73-74, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:272-280, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:489-493).

Codex approval is required through `request_user_input`, but the still-binding host-interaction decision says Default mode forbids that tool for required approvals and directs the coordinator to ask in ordinary chat. This approval path cannot run under the stated host rules (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:149-154, docs/decisions/0061-host-native-human-interaction.md:17-29, docs/decisions/0093-lean-forge-rebuild.md:126-133).

The spec permits edits to Why, Tasks and Notes without new approval, but its roadmap acceptance check rejects a story doc whose approval hash does not match the doc. Migration does not specify a contained preflight for every write and delete, or an interrupted-run retry rule. Those are material for a command removing trees in a client repository under the still-binding path-boundary decision (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:394-416, docs/decisions/0028-path-boundary-invariant.md:37-63, docs/decisions/0093-lean-forge-rebuild.md:126-132).

Carrying an old plan's approval and done-task status is specified only as a conversion result. The source records to trust, how to prove the approved sections are unchanged, and how done tasks survive deletion of old `.factory/` records are not defined (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:400-415).

Source-repo migration and sign-off exemption are selected by the presence of `src/forge/`. A client product could have that path; the spec gives no stronger repository identity check before choosing the delete-nothing mode and bypassing client sign-off (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:156-159, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:422-424).

The proposed success baseline is for close after a clean build, while the target cycle-time metric starts at `forge task start`. No comparable baseline for that metric is supplied (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:605-618).

The principle and criterion say gates refuse only for outcome failures, but the same spec requires refusals for version mismatch, malformed story tables, unrecognized branches and fix file limits (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:26, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:64-65, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:189-194, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:464-469, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:499-502, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:530-538).

The first spec and roadmap cannot be committed through the stated lanes: default-branch commits and branches Forge did not start are refused; a fix touching `docs/specs/` is refused; and a story cannot start without an existing roadmap key (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:79-86, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:119-120, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:189-194, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:277-280).

`forge init` runs `forge sync`, which installs a pre-commit hook refusing default-branch commits, while acceptance criterion 9 requires `forge init` to make the first commit in a repo with no commits. No first-commit exception is given for that hook (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:73-74, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:272-280, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:489-493).

Codex approval is required through `request_user_input`, but the still-binding host-interaction decision says Default mode forbids that tool for required approvals and directs the coordinator to ask in ordinary chat. This approval path cannot run under the stated host rules (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:149-154, docs/decisions/0061-host-native-human-interaction.md:17-29, docs/decisions/0093-lean-forge-rebuild.md:126-133).

The spec permits edits to Why, Tasks and Notes without new approval, but its roadmap acceptance check rejects a story doc whose approval hash does not match the doc. A whole-doc hash would reject those permitted edits; a sections-only hash cannot satisfy the wording of that check (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:144-145, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:460-463, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:505-506).

Each Done-when item is made an instruction to the reviewer, and every task brief carries the entire Done-when list. The confirmed close rule requires unmet items to be P1 findings, so the first task of a multi-task story would be blocked by items assigned to later tasks (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:108-116, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:172-174, docs/specs/close-on-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:77-79).

Human touches are counted in the shared story state file, while the spec says each parallel branch writes only its own state file. It also counts answered questions in the story worktree even though implementation runs in task worktrees, leaving task questions uncounted (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:160-167, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:324-337, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:512-513).

The human may overrule the fix lane and keep work under the limit, but the specified pre-commit and pre-push hooks always refuse a fix that exceeds that limit. No overruling input or exception is defined for the hooks (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:189-198, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:277-285).

The confirmed close rule requires a committed review result containing findings and dismissals. Close marks an item done after CI while a human merges later, but the board timeline puts each merge before 'The story was finished' on the done date. Client migration says the copied manifest identifies the files to delete, but the current manifest records only gate trees and three gate files; it does not inventory the listed docs, workflows, constitution or Codex roles. Migration explicitly deletes client-modified copied files and reports their names only after the change. It specifies no preflight ownership check, preservation or recovery for client additions in mixed-ownership paths, despite the current vendoring contract protecting client skills and workflows (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:400-407, docs/specs/harness-owned-vendoring.md:30-39, factory/scripts/forge_cli/scaffold.py:25-37).

Migration does not specify a contained preflight for every write and delete, or an interrupted-run retry rule. Those are material for a command removing trees in a client repository under the still-binding path-boundary decision (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:394-416, docs/decisions/0028-path-boundary-invariant.md:37-63, docs/decisions/0093-lean-forge-rebuild.md:126-132).

Carrying an old plan's approval and done-task status is specified only as a conversion result. The source records to trust, how to prove the approved sections are unchanged, and how done tasks survive deletion of old `.factory/` records are not defined (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:400-415).

Source-repo migration and sign-off exemption are selected by the presence of `src/forge/`. The proposed success baseline is for close after a clean build, while the target cycle-time metric starts at `forge task start`. No comparable baseline for that metric is supplied (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:605-618).

The principle and criterion say gates refuse only for outcome failures, but the same spec requires refusals for version mismatch, malformed story tables, unrecognized branches and fix file limits (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:26, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:64-65, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:189-194, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:464-469, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:499-502, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:530-538).

The first spec and roadmap cannot be committed through the stated lanes: default-branch commits and branches Forge did not start are refused; a fix touching `docs/specs/` is refused; and a story cannot start without an existing roadmap key (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:79-86, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:119-120, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:189-194, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:277-280).

Codex approval is required through `request_user_input`, but the still-binding host-interaction decision says Default mode forbids that tool for required approvals and directs the coordinator to ask in ordinary chat. The human may overrule the fix lane and keep work under the limit, but the specified pre-commit and pre-push hooks always refuse a fix that exceeds that limit. No overruling input or exception is defined for the hooks (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:189-198, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:277-285).

A task pull request can be opened and merged before `forge close` marks it done, so the specified checks do not make mandatory review unbypassable (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:202-203, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:543-547, docs/decisions/0092-close-is-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:29-36).

The generated host-hook commands have no specified blocking behavior when `forge` cannot launch. The retained portable-hook decision documents that a non-2 launch failure can leave a Claude hook non-blocking and requires an executable health check, while this doctor contract checks drift and installed shims only (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:290-319, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:384-390, docs/decisions/0038-portable-fail-closed-hooks.md:12-19, docs/decisions/0038-portable-fail-closed-hooks.md:22-46).

No command or trigger marks a story done or writes its done date after all task pull requests merge, although story state, the board timeline and success measures require that transition (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:71-88, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:326-328, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:345-352, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:605-609).

Client migration says the copied manifest identifies the files to delete, but the current manifest records only gate trees and three gate files; it does not inventory the listed docs, workflows, constitution or Codex roles. The deletion set and ownership test are therefore undefined for those paths (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:400-407, factory/scripts/check_vendor_integrity.py:23-25, factory/scripts/check_vendor_integrity.py:46-68).

Migration explicitly deletes client-modified copied files and reports their names only after the change. It specifies no preflight ownership check, preservation or recovery for client additions in mixed-ownership paths, despite the current vendoring contract protecting client skills and workflows (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:400-407, docs/specs/harness-owned-vendoring.md:30-39, factory/scripts/forge_cli/scaffold.py:25-37).

Migration does not specify a contained preflight for every write and delete, or an interrupted-run retry rule. Those are material for a command removing trees in a client repository under the still-binding path-boundary decision (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:394-416, docs/decisions/0028-path-boundary-invariant.md:37-63, docs/decisions/0093-lean-forge-rebuild.md:126-132).

Carrying an old plan's approval and done-task status is specified only as a conversion result. The source records to trust, how to prove the approved sections are unchanged, and how done tasks survive deletion of old `.factory/` records are not defined (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:400-415).

Source-repo migration and sign-off exemption are selected by the presence of `src/forge/`. A client product could have that path; the spec gives no stronger repository identity check before choosing the delete-nothing mode and bypassing client sign-off (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:156-159, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:422-424).

The proposed success baseline is for close after a clean build, while the target cycle-time metric starts at `forge task start`. No comparable baseline for that metric is supplied (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:605-618).

The principle and criterion say gates refuse only for outcome failures, but the same spec requires refusals for version mismatch, malformed story tables, unrecognized branches and fix file limits (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:26, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:64-65, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:189-194, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:464-469, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:499-502, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:530-538).

The first spec and roadmap cannot be committed through the stated lanes: default-branch commits and branches Forge did not start are refused; a fix touching `docs/specs/` is refused; and a story cannot start without an existing roadmap key (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:79-86, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:119-120, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:189-194, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:277-280).

`forge init` runs `forge sync`, which installs a pre-commit hook refusing default-branch commits, while acceptance criterion 9 requires `forge init` to make the first commit in a repo with no commits. Codex approval is required through `request_user_input`, but the still-binding host-interaction decision says Default mode forbids that tool for required approvals and directs the coordinator to ask in ordinary chat. This approval path cannot run under the stated host rules (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:149-154, docs/decisions/0061-host-native-human-interaction.md:17-29, docs/decisions/0093-lean-forge-rebuild.md:126-133).

The spec permits edits to Why, Tasks and Notes without new approval, but its roadmap acceptance check rejects a story doc whose approval hash does not match the doc. Each Done-when item is made an instruction to the reviewer, and every task brief carries the entire Done-when list. The confirmed close rule requires unmet items to be P1 findings, so the first task of a multi-task story would be blocked by items assigned to later tasks (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:108-116, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:172-174, docs/specs/close-on-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:77-79).

Human touches are counted in the shared story state file, while the spec says each parallel branch writes only its own state file. It also counts answered questions in the story worktree even though implementation runs in task worktrees, leaving task questions uncounted (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:160-167, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:324-337, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:512-513).

The human may overrule the fix lane and keep work under the limit, but the specified pre-commit and pre-push hooks always refuse a fix that exceeds that limit. No overruling input or exception is defined for the hooks (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:189-198, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:277-285).

The confirmed close rule requires a committed review result containing findings and dismissals. Promotion requires a roadmap key, but no route is specified for adding a newly discovered fix to the roadmap before `forge story new <KEY> --from-fix` can run (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:119-120, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:194-196).

A nonempty `checks` list is insufficient to establish the required full test suite. Neither `forge.toml` nor doctor defines how to verify that the named checks actually run all tests on every pull request (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:60, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:384-390, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:561-563, docs/decisions/0092-close-is-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:39-43, docs/decisions/0092-close-is-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:61-62).

The pull request backstop checks review only when a task or fix is marked done. A task pull request can be opened and merged before `forge close` marks it done, so the specified checks do not make mandatory review unbypassable (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:202-203, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:543-547, docs/decisions/0092-close-is-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:29-36).

The generated host-hook commands have no specified blocking behavior when `forge` cannot launch. The retained portable-hook decision documents that a non-2 launch failure can leave a Claude hook non-blocking and requires an executable health check, while this doctor contract checks drift and installed shims only (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:290-319, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:384-390, docs/decisions/0038-portable-fail-closed-hooks.md:12-19, docs/decisions/0038-portable-fail-closed-hooks.md:22-46).

No command or trigger marks a story done or writes its done date after all task pull requests merge, although story state, the board timeline and success measures require that transition (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:71-88, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:326-328, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:345-352, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:605-609).

Client migration says the copied manifest identifies the files to delete, but the current manifest records only gate trees and three gate files; it does not inventory the listed docs, workflows, constitution or Codex roles. The deletion set and ownership test are therefore undefined for those paths (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:400-407, factory/scripts/check_vendor_integrity.py:23-25, factory/scripts/check_vendor_integrity.py:46-68).

Migration explicitly deletes client-modified copied files and reports their names only after the change. It specifies no preflight ownership check, preservation or recovery for client additions in mixed-ownership paths, despite the current vendoring contract protecting client skills and workflows (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:400-407, docs/specs/harness-owned-vendoring.md:30-39, factory/scripts/forge_cli/scaffold.py:25-37).

Migration does not specify a contained preflight for every write and delete, or an interrupted-run retry rule. Those are material for a command removing trees in a client repository under the still-binding path-boundary decision (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:394-416, docs/decisions/0028-path-boundary-invariant.md:37-63, docs/decisions/0093-lean-forge-rebuild.md:126-132).

Carrying an old plan's approval and done-task status is specified only as a conversion result. The source records to trust, how to prove the approved sections are unchanged, and how done tasks survive deletion of old `.factory/` records are not defined (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:400-415).

Source-repo migration and sign-off exemption are selected by the presence of `src/forge/`. A client product could have that path; the spec gives no stronger repository identity check before choosing the delete-nothing mode and bypassing client sign-off (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:156-159, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:422-424).

The proposed success baseline is for close after a clean build, while the target cycle-time metric starts at `forge task start`. No comparable baseline for that metric is supplied (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:605-618).

The principle and criterion say gates refuse only for outcome failures, but the same spec requires refusals for version mismatch, malformed story tables, unrecognized branches and fix file limits (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:26, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:64-65, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:189-194, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:464-469, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:499-502, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:530-538).

The first spec and roadmap cannot be committed through the stated lanes: default-branch commits and branches Forge did not start are refused; a fix touching `docs/specs/` is refused; and a story cannot start without an existing roadmap key (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:79-86, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:119-120, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:189-194, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:277-280).

`forge init` runs `forge sync`, which installs a pre-commit hook refusing default-branch commits, while acceptance criterion 9 requires `forge init` to make the first commit in a repo with no commits. No first-commit exception is given for that hook (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:73-74, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:272-280, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:489-493).

Codex approval is required through `request_user_input`, but the still-binding host-interaction decision says Default mode forbids that tool for required approvals and directs the coordinator to ask in ordinary chat. This approval path cannot run under the stated host rules (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:149-154, docs/decisions/0061-host-native-human-interaction.md:17-29, docs/decisions/0093-lean-forge-rebuild.md:126-133).

The spec permits edits to Why, Tasks and Notes without new approval, but its roadmap acceptance check rejects a story doc whose approval hash does not match the doc. A whole-doc hash would reject those permitted edits; a sections-only hash cannot satisfy the wording of that check (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:144-145, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:460-463, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:505-506).

Each Done-when item is made an instruction to the reviewer, and every task brief carries the entire Done-when list. The confirmed close rule requires unmet items to be P1 findings, so the first task of a multi-task story would be blocked by items assigned to later tasks (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:108-116, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:172-174, docs/specs/close-on-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:77-79).

Human touches are counted in the shared story state file, while the spec says each parallel branch writes only its own state file. It also counts answered questions in the story worktree even though implementation runs in task worktrees, leaving task questions uncounted (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:160-167, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:324-337, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:512-513).

The human may overrule the fix lane and keep work under the limit, but the specified pre-commit and pre-push hooks always refuse a fix that exceeds that limit. No overruling input or exception is defined for the hooks (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:189-198, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:277-285).

The confirmed close rule requires a committed review result containing findings and dismissals. The v1 state file retains only commit, product tree and clean/blocked status, putting findings and dismissals solely in a mutable pull request body (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:222-224, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:329-337, docs/specs/close-on-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:33-40, docs/specs/close-on-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:80-89).

Close marks an item done after CI while a human merges later, but the board timeline puts each merge before 'The story was finished' on the done date. The specified event order and date order disagree unless a separate post-merge story transition is added (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:202-203, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:225-229, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:349-352).

`forge migrate` uses `forge/migrate-v1` and says it ends through normal close, but the hooks refuse branches without story, task or fix state, and `forge close` is defined only for a task or fix. The migration has no closable item or permitted commit lane (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:81-84, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:277-280, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:394-396).

The switch retains the old test, ticket and roadmap workflows while deleting `factory/`. Those retained workflows call `factory/tests` and `factory/scripts` paths, so their checks would fail after the deletion (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:450-454, .github/workflows/factory-scaffold.yml:53-55, .github/workflows/factory-scaffold.yml:95, .github/workflows/pr-ticket-check.yml:45-59, .github/workflows/roadmap-gate.yml:64-76).

Codex approval is required through `request_user_input`, but the still-binding host-interaction decision says Default mode forbids that tool for required approvals and directs the coordinator to ask in ordinary chat. Each Done-when item is made an instruction to the reviewer, and every task brief carries the entire Done-when list. Human touches are counted in the shared story state file, while the spec says each parallel branch writes only its own state file. The human may overrule the fix lane and keep work under the limit, but the specified pre-commit and pre-push hooks always refuse a fix that exceeds that limit. No overruling input or exception is defined for the hooks (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:189-198, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:277-285).

A task row has no declared write scope, required tests or explicit mapping from its deliverable to Done-when items. Parallel task start has no rule for overlapping changes, branch refresh or reconciliation after one task merges. Dependency readiness alone cannot establish that two task branches can merge safely (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:165-171).

The fix lane supplies only a one-line reason, yet fixes close by the same review rule as tasks. The spec never says what acceptance or test instructions let a reviewer decide that a fix is done (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:184-188, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:202-211, docs/specs/close-on-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:77-92).

The promote rule depends on optional `interfaces` globs, defaulting to an empty list, with no default definition of an interface. Promotion requires a roadmap key, but no route is specified for adding a newly discovered fix to the roadmap before `forge story new <KEY> --from-fix` can run (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:119-120, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:194-196).

A nonempty `checks` list is insufficient to establish the required full test suite. The generated host-hook commands have no specified blocking behavior when `forge` cannot launch. No command or trigger marks a story done or writes its done date after all task pull requests merge, although story state, the board timeline and success measures require that transition (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:71-88, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:326-328, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:345-352, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:605-609).

Client migration says the copied manifest identifies the files to delete, but the current manifest records only gate trees and three gate files; it does not inventory the listed docs, workflows, constitution or Codex roles. Migration explicitly deletes client-modified copied files and reports their names only after the change. Source-repo migration and sign-off exemption are selected by the presence of `src/forge/`. The proposed success baseline is for close after a clean build, while the target cycle-time metric starts at `forge task start`. No comparable baseline for that metric is supplied (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:605-618).

The principle and criterion say gates refuse only for outcome failures, but the same spec requires refusals for version mismatch, malformed story tables, unrecognized branches and fix file limits (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:26, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:64-65, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:189-194, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:464-469, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:499-502, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:530-538).

The first spec and roadmap cannot be committed through the stated lanes: default-branch commits and branches Forge did not start are refused; a fix touching `docs/specs/` is refused; and a story cannot start without an existing roadmap key (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:79-86, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:119-120, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:189-194, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:277-280).

`forge init` runs `forge sync`, which installs a pre-commit hook refusing default-branch commits, while acceptance criterion 9 requires `forge init` to make the first commit in a repo with no commits. Codex approval is required through `request_user_input`, but the still-binding host-interaction decision says Default mode forbids that tool for required approvals and directs the coordinator to ask in ordinary chat. This approval path cannot run under the stated host rules (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:149-154, docs/decisions/0061-host-native-human-interaction.md:17-29, docs/decisions/0093-lean-forge-rebuild.md:126-133).

The spec permits edits to Why, Tasks and Notes without new approval, but its roadmap acceptance check rejects a story doc whose approval hash does not match the doc. A whole-doc hash would reject those permitted edits; a sections-only hash cannot satisfy the wording of that check (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:144-145, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:460-463, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:505-506).

Each Done-when item is made an instruction to the reviewer, and every task brief carries the entire Done-when list. The confirmed close rule requires unmet items to be P1 findings, so the first task of a multi-task story would be blocked by items assigned to later tasks (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:108-116, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:172-174, docs/specs/close-on-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:77-79).

Human touches are counted in the shared story state file, while the spec says each parallel branch writes only its own state file. The human may overrule the fix lane and keep work under the limit, but the specified pre-commit and pre-push hooks always refuse a fix that exceeds that limit. No overruling input or exception is defined for the hooks (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:189-198, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:277-285).

The confirmed close rule requires a committed review result containing findings and dismissals. The specified event order and date order disagree unless a separate post-merge story transition is added (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:202-203, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:225-229, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:349-352).

`forge migrate` uses `forge/migrate-v1` and says it ends through normal close, but the hooks refuse branches without story, task or fix state, and `forge close` is defined only for a task or fix. The spec does not define how the amended hash and complete finding dispositions are validated before approval, despite the confirmed close contract requiring both read and amended hashes (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:126-128, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:138-145, docs/specs/close-on-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:50-54, docs/specs/close-on-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:106-107).

Approval capture does not specify the retained Codex trust checks for the exact current digest, runtime, tool identity, replay refusal and one eligible candidate. Matching a short hash alone leaves those required checks to the implementer to guess (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:149-154, docs/decisions/0082-codex-hook-trust-boundary.md:17-22).

The story doc, read notes and approval state are written in a story worktree, but no step commits them before task branches are created from the story branch. An uncommitted story doc cannot reach the first task pull request by branching from that branch (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:119-128, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:165-170).

A task row has no declared write scope, required tests or explicit mapping from its deliverable to Done-when items. Close is nevertheless required to give Autoreview the task's scope and required-test audit instructions (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:100-116, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:172-175, docs/specs/close-on-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:33-36, docs/specs/close-on-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:90-92).

Parallel task start has no rule for overlapping changes, branch refresh or reconciliation after one task merges. Dependency readiness alone cannot establish that two task branches can merge safely (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:165-171).

The fix lane supplies only a one-line reason, yet fixes close by the same review rule as tasks. The spec never says what acceptance or test instructions let a reviewer decide that a fix is done (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:184-188, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:202-211, docs/specs/close-on-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:77-92).

The promote rule depends on optional `interfaces` globs, defaulting to an empty list, with no default definition of an interface. An API or data-contract change can therefore remain a fix despite the accepted decision requiring interface changes to become stories (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:61, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:189-194, docs/decisions/0093-lean-forge-rebuild.md:40-42).

Promotion requires a roadmap key, but no route is specified for adding a newly discovered fix to the roadmap before `forge story new <KEY> --from-fix` can run (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:119-120, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:194-196).

A nonempty `checks` list is insufficient to establish the required full test suite. Neither `forge.toml` nor doctor defines how to verify that the named checks actually run all tests on every pull request (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:60, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:384-390, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:561-563, docs/decisions/0092-close-is-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:39-43, docs/decisions/0092-close-is-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:61-62).

The pull request backstop checks review only when a task or fix is marked done. A task pull request can be opened and merged before `forge close` marks it done, so the specified checks do not make mandatory review unbypassable (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:202-203, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:543-547, docs/decisions/0092-close-is-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:29-36).

The generated host-hook commands have no specified blocking behavior when `forge` cannot launch. The retained portable-hook decision documents that a non-2 launch failure can leave a Claude hook non-blocking and requires an executable health check, while this doctor contract checks drift and installed shims only (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:290-319, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:384-390, docs/decisions/0038-portable-fail-closed-hooks.md:12-19, docs/decisions/0038-portable-fail-closed-hooks.md:22-46).

No command or trigger marks a story done or writes its done date after all task pull requests merge, although story state, the board timeline and success measures require that transition (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:71-88, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:326-328, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:345-352, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:605-609).

Client migration says the copied manifest identifies the files to delete, but the current manifest records only gate trees and three gate files; it does not inventory the listed docs, workflows, constitution or Codex roles. The deletion set and ownership test are therefore undefined for those paths (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:400-407, factory/scripts/check_vendor_integrity.py:23-25, factory/scripts/check_vendor_integrity.py:46-68).

Migration explicitly deletes client-modified copied files and reports their names only after the change. It specifies no preflight ownership check, preservation or recovery for client additions in mixed-ownership paths, despite the current vendoring contract protecting client skills and workflows (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:400-407, docs/specs/harness-owned-vendoring.md:30-39, factory/scripts/forge_cli/scaffold.py:25-37).

Migration does not specify a contained preflight for every write and delete, or an interrupted-run retry rule. Those are material for a command removing trees in a client repository under the still-binding path-boundary decision (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:394-416, docs/decisions/0028-path-boundary-invariant.md:37-63, docs/decisions/0093-lean-forge-rebuild.md:126-132).

Carrying an old plan's approval and done-task status is specified only as a conversion result. The source records to trust, how to prove the approved sections are unchanged, and how done tasks survive deletion of old `.factory/` records are not defined (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:400-415).

Source-repo migration and sign-off exemption are selected by the presence of `src/forge/`. A client product could have that path; the spec gives no stronger repository identity check before choosing the delete-nothing mode and bypassing client sign-off (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:156-159, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:422-424).

The proposed success baseline is for close after a clean build, while the target cycle-time metric starts at `forge task start`. No comparable baseline for that metric is supplied (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:605-618).

The principle and criterion say gates refuse only for outcome failures, but the same spec requires refusals for version mismatch, malformed story tables, unrecognized branches and fix file limits (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:26, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:64-65, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:189-194, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:464-469, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:499-502, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:530-538).

The first spec and roadmap cannot be committed through the stated lanes: default-branch commits and branches Forge did not start are refused; a fix touching `docs/specs/` is refused; and a story cannot start without an existing roadmap key (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:79-86, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:119-120, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:189-194, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:277-280).

`forge init` runs `forge sync`, which installs a pre-commit hook refusing default-branch commits, while acceptance criterion 9 requires `forge init` to make the first commit in a repo with no commits. No first-commit exception is given for that hook (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:73-74, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:272-280, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:489-493).

Codex approval is required through `request_user_input`, but the still-binding host-interaction decision says Default mode forbids that tool for required approvals and directs the coordinator to ask in ordinary chat. This approval path cannot run under the stated host rules (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:149-154, docs/decisions/0061-host-native-human-interaction.md:17-29, docs/decisions/0093-lean-forge-rebuild.md:126-133).

The spec permits edits to Why, Tasks and Notes without new approval, but its roadmap acceptance check rejects a story doc whose approval hash does not match the doc. A whole-doc hash would reject those permitted edits; a sections-only hash cannot satisfy the wording of that check (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:144-145, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:460-463, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:505-506).

Each Done-when item is made an instruction to the reviewer, and every task brief carries the entire Done-when list. The confirmed close rule requires unmet items to be P1 findings, so the first task of a multi-task story would be blocked by items assigned to later tasks (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:108-116, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:172-174, docs/specs/close-on-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:77-79).

Human touches are counted in the shared story state file, while the spec says each parallel branch writes only its own state file. It also counts answered questions in the story worktree even though implementation runs in task worktrees, leaving task questions uncounted (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:160-167, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:324-337, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:512-513).

The human may overrule the fix lane and keep work under the limit, but the specified pre-commit and pre-push hooks always refuse a fix that exceeds that limit. No overruling input or exception is defined for the hooks (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:189-198, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:277-285).

The confirmed close rule requires a committed review result containing findings and dismissals. The v1 state file retains only commit, product tree and clean/blocked status, putting findings and dismissals solely in a mutable pull request body (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:222-224, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:329-337, docs/specs/close-on-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:33-40, docs/specs/close-on-green-ci-and-clean-review.md:80-89).

Close marks an item done after CI while a human merges later, but the board timeline puts each merge before 'The story was finished' on the done date. The specified event order and date order disagree unless a separate post-merge story transition is added (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:202-203, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:225-229, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:349-352).

`forge migrate` uses `forge/migrate-v1` and says it ends through normal close, but the hooks refuse branches without story, task or fix state, and `forge close` is defined only for a task or fix. The migration has no closable item or permitted commit lane (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:81-84, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:277-280, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:394-396).

The switch retains the old test, ticket and roadmap workflows while deleting `factory/`. Those retained workflows call `factory/tests` and `factory/scripts` paths, so their checks would fail after the deletion (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:450-454, .github/workflows/factory-scaffold.yml:53-55, .github/workflows/factory-scaffold.yml:95, .github/workflows/pr-ticket-check.yml:45-59, .github/workflows/roadmap-gate.yml:64-76).

The FDE story must run end to end before the switch, but its approved plan requires `forge payback`, `forge spec measure`, `forge doctor --fix` and a dated check-back. The v1 command table omits those commands and places the FDE features outside this spec until that story ships, making the stated switch check unreachable as written (docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:69-88, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:445-446, docs/specs/lean-forge-v1.md:623-629, plans/active/FORGE-FDE-1-the-agent-works-as-a-forward-deployed-engineer-gstack-removed.md:17-24, plans/active/FORGE-FDE-1-the-agent-works-as-a-forward-deployed-engineer-gstack-removed.md:29-35).
